chunks: A number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Al-Washshāʾ, from Dāwūd al-Ḥammār, from Ibn Abī Yaʿfūr, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

I heard him saying: ‘There are three whom Allah will not speak to on the Day of Resurrection, nor will He purify them, and for them is a painful punishment: one who claims an Imamate from Allah which does not belong to him, one who rejects an Imam from Allah, and one who alleges that those two have a share in Islam.’

key_terms.إِمَامَةً: the divinely appointed office of leadership and authority
key_terms.نَصِيبًا: a share or portion; here, a valid standing within Islam
key_terms.يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ: the Day of Resurrection when people are judged
key_terms.يُزَكِّيهِمْ: He purifies them; meaning Allah does not cleanse or vindicate them

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith say about falsely claiming the Imamate or rejecting a true Imam?
ai.summary: This hadith condemns false claims to divinely appointed religious authority and the rejection of the true Imam appointed by Allah. It presents both acts as grave deviations with severe consequences in the Hereafter, emphasizing the centrality of Imamate in faith and religious legitimacy.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Washa, from Dawood Al Hammar, from Ibn Abu Yafour, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said,

‘I heard him<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘Three (people), Allah<sup>azwj</sup> will not be Speaking to them on the Day of Judgment, nor will He<sup>azwj</sup> be Purifying them, and for them would be a painful Punishment – the one who alleges that he is an Imam (Appointed by) Allah<sup>azwj</sup> but it (the Imamate) isn’t for him, and the one who denies an Imam<sup>asws</sup> from Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, and the one who claims that there is a share for the two of them (number one and number two) in Al-Islam’.
en.sarwar: 4. A number of our people has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Washsha’ from Dawud al-Himar from ibn abu Ya‘fur who has said the following. “I heard abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) say, ‘On the Day of Judgment Allah will not speak to them, He will not purify them and for them there will be painful suffering. He said it three time. (He added) they are those who claim to be the Imam with Divine authority and, in fact, he is not so, those who reject the Imam who possesses Divine authority and those who think that the two has a share in Islam.”
